question: In adults with hypertension, heart failure, coronary artery disease, recent myocardial infarction, kidney disease (diabetic or non-diabetic) or high cardiovascular risk, how do ACE inhibitors compare with each other and with placebo or other treatments in effectiveness and harms?
eligibility: Adults with hypertension, heart failure, coronary artery disease, recent myocardial infarction or left ventricular dysfunction, diabetic or non-diabetic kidney disease, or high cardiovascular risk.

An ACE inhibitor (for example benazepril, captopril, enalapril, fosinopril, lisinopril, moexipril, perindopril, quinapril, ramipril or trandolapril) compared with another ACE inhibitor, placebo or another treatment.
Clinical outcomes (mortality, cardiovascular events, hospitalisation, kidney disease progression, quality of life) or adverse events.
Randomized controlled trials; controlled observational studies for harms.
as_of_source: Day after latest Entrez date among included SYNERGY records (lower bound).
source: Cohen et al. 2006 screening collection, ACEInhibitors SYNERGY subset (41 included PubMed IDs): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asreview/systematic-review-datasets/metadata-v1-final/datasets/Cohen_2006/output/online/ACEInhibitors.csv; source paper DOI https://doi.org/10.1197/jamia.M1929
notes: Question and eligibility reconstructed from the Drug Effectiveness Review Project (Oregon EPC) drug-class review this subset came from, not from its original protocol. The Cohen 2006 collection drew citations from a 1994-2003 MEDLINE subset (TREC 2004 Genomics), so gold covers 1994-2003 only: recall is valid, but result counts include earlier literature. The answer key uses label_included PubMed IDs (article-level inclusion).
